text: Why is the naive Fibonacci a poor teaching example despite being the standard one?
choices: It requires understanding of the golden ratio
It is too difficult for beginners
It cannot be written in Java
It is faithful to the definition and catastrophically wrong as an implementation
explanation: It is beautiful, matches the mathematics exactly, and is unusable beyond small inputs. Elegance that helps reveals the problem's structure; elegance admired for itself is a different thing, and presenting this one as an exemplar teaches the wrong lesson.
